title: Caviar, kamerasız ve mat titanyum kaplamalı özel iPhone Duo modelini tanıttı
summary: Özel tasarım ürünleriyle bilinen Caviar, kamera modülü tamamen kaldırılan ve fiyatı 13.990 dolardan başlayan sınırlı sayıdaki iPhone Duo modelini duyurdu.
body:
Yanko Design'ın aktardığına göre, lüks tasarımlarıyla tanınan Caviar Global, Apple'ın katlanabilir cihazı **iPhone Duo** modelini temel alan son derece sıra dışı ve kamarasız bir versiyon geliştirdi. Şirket, gizlilik ve minimalizm odaklı bu özel cihaz için 14.000 dolara yakın bir fiyat etiketi belirledi ve sadece 19 adet üretim yapacağını açıkladı.

## Kamerasız ve tamamen düz titanyum gövde

Cihazın arkasındaki ve önündeki tüm kamera modülleri ile delikler tamamen ortadan kaldırıldı. Bu sayede arka panel, parıltılı saten bitişli siyah titanyumdan oluşan kesintisiz ve düz bir yüzeye dönüştü. Apple'ın ekran altı yerine çerçeveye yerleştirdiği Touch ID teknolojisi sayesinde kameraların çıkarılması telefonun kilit açma işlevini engellemiyor. İç ekranda da hiçbir delik veya çentik bulunmuyor.

## Özel kutu içeriği ve sınırlı üretim

Sadece 512 GB depolama seçeneğiyle gelen ve fiyatı 13.990 dolar olarak belirlenen cihaz, kilitlenebilir siyah lüks bir kutuda sahiplerine ulaştırılıyor. Kutu içerisinde ayrıca altın kaplama hatıra bir madeni para da yer alıyor. Cihazın çerçevesine özel seri numaraları da işlenmiş durumda.

**Neden önemli?** Caviar, pazarın en pahalı akıllı telefonlarından birini bazı temel özelliklerini tamamen sökerek çok daha yüksek bir fiyatla ve sınırlı sayıda sunmasıyla dikkat çekiyor.

source_texts.title: Would you pay $14,000 for an iPhone Duo without any cameras?
source_texts.summary: Would you pay $14,000 for an iPhone Duo without any cameras? Imagine sitting at a table with friends and whipping your phone out. Your friends see it’s a foldable… then as you unfold it, the animation...
source_texts.text:
Imagine sitting at a table with friends and whipping your phone out. Your friends see it’s a foldable… then as you unfold it, the animation looks suspiciously like the iPhone Duo. Your friends are impressed, they designate you as the group photo taker… and you tell them regrettably that your iPhone Duo has no cameras. Then you add… not only does it not sport any cameras, it also costs fourteen grand.
To be honest, that scenario is entirely imaginary. Mainly for a bunch of key reasons. Caviar built this version of the iPhone Duo for privacy, championing what they call “Privacy, Minimalism, and a Refined Masculine Style.” Someone who sees truth in that ethos isn’t designated photographer material. And if they were, shelling 14k on a phone means you probably have a few extra grand to hire a photographer wherever you go. The only reason someone buys this hare-brained version of the iPhone Duo is because they can. Plain and simple.
Designer: Caviar Global
Removing the camera stack from the back of the iPhone Duo does something unexpected: the phone becomes genuinely beautiful. That rear panel, normally dominated by the triple-lens module, turns into a single flat sheet of satin-finished black titanium. No bumps, no rings, no glass circles competing for visual real estate, just one uninterrupted surface that shifts character depending on the light hitting it. Caviar calls the inspiration “supersonic aviation aesthetics,” which sounds like marketing speak until you actually look at the product photos. A blacked-out Apple logo sits flush in the titanium, the Caviar crown marks the opposite panel in a swept fabric-like texture, and the whole thing looks less like a phone and more like a prop from a very expensive spy film.
Apple’s decision to use Touch ID for the iPhone Duo, abandoning Face ID, turns out to be what makes Caviar’s camera-free execution actually hold up. A Face ID phone needs its front camera array to function as a biometric sensor, so pulling that out would mean a very pretty device that cannot unlock. Touch ID lives in the frame rather than behind the screen, so Caviar could strip the entire camera stack, front hole-punch and rear module both, without breaking anything fundamental. Based on product images, the inner display on the Ultimate appears completely clean, no hole-punch interrupting the screen, which makes the inside as seamless as the outside. Two separate design decisions from two separate companies ended up fitting together better than either could have planned.
Caviar made 19 of these total. Each unit ships in a custom lockable black luxury box, presented the way a jeweler presents a watch rather than the way Apple ships a phone. A smaller gold-colored wooden case inside holds what appears to be a gold-plated commemorative coin, the kind of object that exists purely to make the unboxing feel like a ceremony. The side of the phone is engraved with a serial number too, for exclusivity. Caviar knows exactly who they are selling to, and made sure the packaging matches the energy.
Caviar has been doing this for years, taking flagship Apple hardware somewhere Apple would never go, for clients who appreciate the gesture. The formula is consistent: start with the most premium Apple product on the market, make it rarer, make it more dramatic, and let the price be the final statement. We have covered their gold-plated and titanium iPhone builds here before, and none of them committed this hard to stripping features as a form of self-expression. At $13,990 for 19 units (mind you, that’s just the 512GB variant), the Ultimate is the purest version of the Caviar argument: a phone that costs seven times its base price because it does less, and somehow makes that sound like the point.

source_texts.title: Apple has a genius, but obvious solution for the iPhone Duo’s long-term display crease visibility
source_texts.summary: The iPhone Duo has a cover layer that'll cost just $19 to replace under warranty, Apple says.
source_texts.text:
Apple has revealed that the iPhone Duo’s inner display has a replaceable cover layer that will enable foldable phone owners to negate the innate increase in visibility of the display crease that tends to get worse with increased usage.
In an interview with TikToker Angelica Siciliani Fendi (@AngieTurorials) Kate Bergeron, Apple VP of Hardware Engineering revealed that the iPhone Duo display can regain a day one feel with a seemingly quick replacement of the cover layer atop the matte display coating.
Bergeron said: “The matte display coating does a really nice job of, I’ll say minimising the crease. But there’s a cover layer on top, and we’ve done a significant amount of engineering work to help that wear in as long of a manner as we can, and to make sure that you get the most out of that layer’s performance. It’s actually replaceable, which is a really nice thing for the customer, that you can peel off that layer and get a new one.”
Better still, it feels like the replacement will be really affordable, with the company charging $19 with Apple Care to replace the cover layer. As 9to5Mac points out in its reporting, it’s not clear how much it’ll cost without the warranty.
That might convince some users who are in two minds about buying an iPhone Duo for fears it may start to use its lustre over time.
Apple will open pre-orders for the iPhone Duo on October 16. It is thought the company will have quite limited supplies out of the gate.
